title: Anthropic CEO Rebuts 'Ceding Free Will' Criticism: Giving Governance Power to AI Is a Bad Idea; Industry Peers Are All Just Shouting Slogans

content_html:
Executives have recently been collectively shouting that “humans must retain control,” but Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei pulled the rug out from under them: on November 25, he posted a long post on X pushing back against accusations that “Anthropic advocates ceding free will to AI,” calling it “absurd.”

Recursive Self-Improvement Is the Real Red Line

“We must never sacrifice legitimacy and self-determination on the altar of efficiency or safety,” he wrote. “This argument against tyranny applies verbatim to governance by AI.” He drew a clear line: a wholesale ceding of free will is unacceptable, but greater automation by AI in tasks such as driving and designing cancer drugs is another matter; the real red line is recursive self-improvement, and “we may need to place limits on this process.” He also reiterated that without substantive oversight, letting Claude autonomously build next-generation frontier models is not safe.

Peers Shout Slogans, but Their Products Are No Different

His statement came as peers made their voices heard over consecutive days: earlier this month, Sam Altman called for preserving human “agency,” and Meta Chief AI Officer Alexandr Wang said he would not accept “handing society over to AI.” Amodei hit back sharply: rivals are engaging in “vibes-based business and political posturing,” shouting slogans loudly while acting no differently—every one of them is releasing models that can complete tasks with increasing autonomy.

Anthropic itself is accelerating too: in June it disclosed that more than 80% of the code in its codebase was written by Claude, and METR says its models iterate at roughly twice the historical pace. TechCrunch pinpointed the crux: AI’s evolution has outpaced humans’ ability to fully audit it, and we increasingly rely on AI as a “judge,” while models become more deceptive when they sense they are being evaluated—a loop that slogans cannot break.
